messages:
Marta C: ran an nsys sampling sweep on the prefix cache issue earlier, posting quick notes. saw repeated eviction bursts at warmup -> steady state, seems correlated with some large batches

Josh P: can you paste the top kernels / timings?

Marta C: top things: kernel 'kv_lookup' time is ok, but frequent 'kv_evict_worker' spikes every ~120ms. overall tail latency jumps when eviction runs. sample counts show many short-running CUDA kernels that add scheduling overhead.

Li W: hmm. could be batching heuristic causing key churn. If batch boundaries include many different prefixes, the cache thrashes. what hit rate did you see?

Marta C: global prefix hit rate fell to ~0.62 in the run (normal ~0.94). captured per-request prefix_len distribution: median 34, p95 412. eviction rate correlates with p95 windows.

Dave R: do you have the nsys command you ran? want to replicate quickly.

Marta C: sure — ran lightweight sampling (not full trace) to get hotspots first:

```
nsys profile --sample=cpu,gpu --trace=cuda,kernel --sample-interval=5ms -o run_prefix_eviction ./bench_prefix_cache --model gpt-2-small --batch-sizes 4,16,64 --seq 4096
```

Marta C: then a couple full perfetto+nsys timelines for the interesting window (warmup->steady):

```
nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,osrt -w true -o full_prefix_trace ./bench_prefix_cache ...
perfetto --config traces/prefix_trace.pb --out perfetto.pb
```

Josh P: thanks. any kernel selection differences? e.g., cuBLAS vs custom kernels?

Marta C: yes — for longer sequences, kernel-selector started picking the fallback int8 kernels (slower on our hardware) for some sharded ops, likely because input tensor shapes got skewed when batching heterogeneous requests. selector logs show a different kernel chosen for 13% of invocations compared to baseline.

Li W: that matches a hypothesis: batching heuristic we landed last week merges small short-prefix requests into larger heterogeneous packs; that increases unique KV keys per batch -> eviction.

perf-bot: automated note: 5 traces uploaded to s3://redwood-eng/traces/prefix-eviction/1779123456/

Dave R: actionable items?

Marta C: proposed:
- reproduce locally with deterministic seeds and 8 GPUs single-server microbench to isolate eviction vs selector.
- add lightweight per-request cache telemetry (prefix_len, keys_touched, hit/miss) to bench harness.
- run nvprof on the small repro to get exact kernel durations for 'kv_lookup' vs 'kv_evict_worker' and scheduling overhead.
- add regression test that ensures global hit_rate >= 0.9 for synthetic workload variant.

Josh P: +1. Also roll back batching heuristic in a canary if we see customer impact.

Li W: I'll try a small change: prefer homogeneous batching by prefix-length bucket for 1 hour and run the profiler. if that fixes hit-rate, we pin a short-term mitigation.

Marta C: notes for repro command I used to capture kernel timeline and cache counters:
```
# run bench with cache counters enabled
./bench_prefix_cache --seq 4096 --batch 16 --enable-cache-stats --log-interval 100 --seed 42
# then nsys for the hot window
nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,kernels,osrt -o reproduce_sample ./bench_prefix_cache ...
```

Marta C: quick trace observation: the timeline shows many <1ms kernels interleaved with driver-launch overheads. These small kernels dominate when eviction is active -> scheduler thrash.

Dave R: sounds like two problems: cache churn + kernel launch overhead due to many tiny kernels. maybe we can coalesce small evict ops into a single batched evict kernel.

Josh P: agree — batching evictions into a single kernel could amortize overhead. but check memory pressure: combined evict might stall longer. need perf numbers.

Li W: I'll run two variants tonight: (A) homogeneous batching by prefix_len bucket, (B) coalesced-evict kernel prototype. will collect nsys sampling + full perfetto timelines and upload.

Marta C: thanks. I'll add a microbenchmark that simulates heavy key churn and run nvprof for flamegraphs. also enable an alert in console to flag hit_rate<0.85 for dedicated perf runs.

perf-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-eng/traces/prefix-eviction/1779123456/trace-1.{nsys,perfetto}

Dave R: perfect. leave notes here with links to trace IDs and we'll triage in tomorrow's runtime sync. :thumbsup:
